chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ, from al-Sakūnī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: May I perform salat (prayer) on the shādhakūnah when janabah has affected it? He said: “There is no harm.”

Then the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—said: There is no harm in performing salat (prayer) in the khuff even if there is najasah in it, and likewise the sandal; though keeping away from that is better. And when a person steps with his sandal or khuff on najasah, then wipes them with dust, they become tahir by that.
That is indicated by the following.

key_terms.الشَّاذَكُونَةِ: a type of spread or cloth on which one may sit or perform salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity referred to here as affecting the item
key_terms.الْخُفِّ: leather footwear or khuff worn on the foot
key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with dust or earth, used here as a means of purification
key_terms.طَهُرَا: they became tahir, meaning ritually pure
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) on a surface affected by janabah or in footwear that has najasah?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to taharah and salat (prayer), stating that praying on a surface affected by janabah is permitted. It also states that praying in khuffs or sandals is not problematic even if najasah is present, while avoiding such cases is preferable, and that wiping footwear with dust after stepping on najasah purifies it.
